subject: Medford Residential and ADU Zoning Reform
overview: The board opened a public hearing on new Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) regulations and continued its review of comprehensive residential zoning updates. After extensive public testimony, the board voted to continue the hearings to July 9th and established a multi-month schedule for deliberation and additional feedback.

items.title: ADU and Residential Zoning Districts Hearing
items.summary: Opened a new public hearing to align local ADU rules with state law and continued the hearing on proposed Neighborhood and Urban Residential zoning amendments. Consultants presented analyses on lot coverage, setbacks, and density across five proposed districts, noting that topography and private ways will restrict growth in certain neighborhoods.

items.title: Public Comment
items.summary: Heard from dozens of residents who were divided between supporting increased density to mitigate the housing crisis and requesting a pause to study impacts on infrastructure, schools, and emergency services. Several speakers criticized the notification process and asked for neighborhood-specific analyses before moving the proposal forward.

items.title: Hearing Continuance and Schedule Adoption
items.summary: Approved a motion to continue the hearings for ADU and residential zoning updates to July 9th. The board adopted a schedule setting a July 16th deadline for written public comments and planning for board deliberations through September, with a target for final recommendations in October.

items.title: Recognitions and Adjournment
items.summary: Recognized Director Alicia Hunt for receiving a leadership award for the Clippership Connector and board member Peter Calves for earning his professional engineer license; approved adjournment.
